in_text_mentions: ctopic pheochromocytoma located at one side of the abdominal aorta. Computed tomography (CT) of adrenal gland was performed in 10 patients. The images revealed uneven mass with intact capsules (Figure 1) and they were more obvious on enhanced CT images (Figure 2). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in 4 patients and the images showed even or uneven masses with intact capsules. Thyroid B-mode ultrasonography was performed in 13 patients and revealed low echogenic regions with uneven echo. Thyroid CT was performed in 10 patients and showed inhomogeneous low density images (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Patient CT image with captioned adrenal pheochromocytoma, a classic MEN2A manifestation. B: Patient CT image with captioned adrenal pheochromocytoma in an MEN2A case. C: Human histopathology panel captioned as pheochromocytoma, a specific MEN2A manifestation. D: Thyroid immunohistochemistry is calcitonin-positive and the text confirms medullary thyroid carcinoma in MEN2A; amyloid-rich histology is not explicitly shown, so a proposed finding is used.

panels.figure_caption: Results of CT and histopathological examination. A: Coronal CT image. B: Sagittal CT image. The red arrows indicate pheochromcytoma. C: H&E staining (40×) of pheochromcytoma. D: Immunohistochemical staining of thyroid sections: calcitonin (+).
in_text_mentions: (6.0×6.2×5.0 cm), which was confirmed as phaeochromcytoma by histopathological examination during and after surgery. US disclosed bilateral thyroid nodule containing calcifications. The patient underwent total right thyroidectomy and 70% left thyroidectomy. Histopathology of the surgical specimens of the thyroid gland was positive for medullary thyroid carcinoma. Immunohistochemical staining displayed calcitonin (+), TG(-), TTF1(-), CgA(-), CK19(-) and Syn(-). Calcitonin was 26.1 pg/mL 2 months after surgery. The results of CT scanning, H&E staining and immunohistochemistry are shown in Fig 2.

findings.label: Adrenal pheochromocytoma
findings.evidence: Caption states enhanced accumulation of 123I-MIBG in bilateral adrenal masses; in-text confirms increased MIBG uptake in bilateral adrenal masses in a patient diagnosed with MEN2A-related bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma

panels.rationale: Single-panel 123I-MIBG scintigraphy of a human patient with confirmed multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A, showing bilateral enhanced radiotracer uptake corresponding to adrenal pheochromocytomas, with red arrow annotations marking the masses; no excluded content types are present.
panels.attribution_text: Yanagida et al. Advanced disease and biochemical phenotype shift in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A-related pheochromocytoma.. JCEM case reports 2026. doi:10.1210/jcemcr/luag038. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: 123I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy. Enhanced accumulation of MIBG in the adrenal masses was observed bilaterally.
in_text_mentions: tion was 39.8 Hounsfield units (HU) for the right adrenal mass and 44.7 HU for the left adrenal mass. There was no evidence of invasion of the surrounding tissues by either mass (Fig. 2). 123I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy showed increased accumulation in the adrenal masses bilaterally. There was no accumulation in distant organs (Fig. 3). Based on the above, the patient was diagnosed with MEN2A-related bilateral adrenal pheochromocytoma (cT1N0M0, cStage I), and medullary thyroid carcinoma (cT1aN0M0, cStage I). We decided to prioritize surgical resection of the pheochromocytoma.

plate_findings.evidence: H&E histopathology shows small round blue cells in the tumor; stated to be consistent with medullary thyroid carcinoma in a MEN2A case

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient H&E histology from a MEN2A case showing medullary thyroid carcinoma/C-cell carcinoma morphology; disease attribution is supported by the article title and the in-text statement that the findings were consistent with MTC. B: Calcitonin IHC from the same MEN2A case confirms the C-cell/medullary thyroid carcinoma phenotype; included as an immunohistochemical manifestation of the configured disease.
panels.attribution_text: Yang. A Case Study of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2A.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.27504. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology Hematoxylin and eosin (A) at 400x magnification. Calcitonin immunohistochemcial stain (B) at 400x magnification.
in_text_mentions: Histochemical investigation with hematoxylin and eosin shows small round blue cells along with immunohistochemical staining for calcitonin being positive in the tumor (Figure 2A, 2B). These results were consistent with MTC. Medullary carcinoma was also found to be in three lymph nodes removed from the central neck dissection as well as one level III lymph node on the left.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Real patient histology image from a multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A patient showing characteristic small nest (zellballen) proliferation of adrenal pheochromocytoma tumor cells on HE staining. B: Real patient histology image from a multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A patient showing venous invasion, a feature of malignant biological behavior of the adrenal pheochromocytoma, on HE staining. C: Real patient histology image from a multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A patient showing partial extracapsular invasion, a feature of malignant potential of the adrenal pheochromocytoma, on HE staining. D: Real patient immunohistochemistry image from a multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A patient showing Ki-67 labeling index of 10%, indicating elevated proliferative activity of the adrenal pheochromocytoma.

Because no thermal damage or other surgical artifacts were identified, these findings were considered to reflect the tumor's biological malignancy rather than surgical manipulation.
